name: Whittemore Center Arena
use: Hockey arena (men's and women's ice hockey), concerts, commencement and large events
builtText: construction began Nov 12, 1994; opened Nov 1995; dedicated May 5, 1996
statusNote: Hockey renovation project announced 2023; status unconfirmed

renovations.what: $6M renovation: ice reduced from 200x100 to 200x90 ft, new glass, NHL-style boards, sound system
UNH Hockey Renovation Project announced: larger accessible locker rooms, expanded strength and conditioning, offices; goal $16M ($4M gift + $6M state); groundbreaking tentatively 2025

facts.text: Construction began November 12, 1994; the arena opened in November 1995 and was dedicated May 5, 1996, named for Frederick B. Whittemore, who gave $1.5 million toward it.
Built for $30 million; it replaced the adjacent Snively Arena as home of UNH hockey.
The rink was a full Olympic-size 200x100 ft sheet until a 2022 renovation reduced it to 200x90 ft.
UNH had invested nearly $14 million in recent years in the ice surface, audio/visual technology and part of the HVAC before the 2023 hockey renovation project.
The NH House of Representatives met in the arena in 2020 for social distancing.

verdict: 1995 hockey arena with a glass entrance and curved flank; a loud, well-loved home ice, freshened in 2022.
notes: Whether the hockey renovation broke ground in 2025 or is complete is NOT confirmed (latest source: UNH Magazine Winter 2024, 'tentatively scheduled for 2025'). Sources disagree on project size ($16M goal; search snippets mention $20M/$23M). Architect not found. Capacity (old row 6,501) not re-verified this pass. Old row's Stadium Journey 3.86 and 'frankly unsafe' boards quote not re-verified. The archives paragraph says the Whittemore Center 'houses the Hamel Recreation Center' (outdated wording). Photos: long low grey concrete-and-glass arena with a band of clerestory glazing and a square entrance tower; utilitarian. Licensed photos (2013, 2024): long low concrete-and-glass arena with a curving metal roof edge, ribbon clerestory glazing and a square entrance tower, fronted by the green field-hockey turf; tidy but generic. Interior not photographed. Licensed interior added: a 2008 Flickr photo of the arena bowl shows exposed steel roof trusses over steep bench seating.
judgeNotes: Photos show a tidy, generic arena. Exterior up a point from the old run.
